content:
A survey of thousands of 9to5Mac readers has shown that even the most loyal Apple customers may extend their upgrade cycles following the company's price increases.

Among the responses, "upgrading less frequently" was the most popular choice, with only 9% of respondents saying the price hikes would not affect their purchasing behaviour……

As we noted before, some products saw increases of more than 50%, while memory and storage upgrades doubled in cost in some cases — and there's no sign of this letting up anytime soon.

If you were looking for a group to keep buying Apple products at higher prices no matter what, you might have expected 9to5Mac readers to be that group. But Friday's poll shows even these loyal fans have their limits.

Over 90% of readers said they would change their buying habits due to the price hikes, with more than a third saying they would upgrade less frequently.

  • Upgrade less often: 38%
  • Wait for a sale: 14%
  • Give up one or more Apple products: 12%
  • Buy a lower-tier model: 9%
  • No impact: 9%

A reader commented:

Of course, new features could always change consumers' minds, but this result at least gives hope that Apple will see sales slow down, and might trim pricing slightly to maintain demand.
